open_obligations: Note that the doubly-efficient setting covers time-T computations, not all of PSPACE with an efficient honest prover.
Check that the oracle model of human judgement corresponds to Irving et al.'s polynomial-time judge H.
Check the role of O(S log T) verifier time when S is large.
out.other_title: Theorem 1: debate with a polynomial-time judge and optimal play decides PSPACE
out.rationale: Irving et al.'s Theorem 1 shows polynomial-step debate with a polynomial-time judge decides PSPACE when debaters are unbounded. Brown-Cohen et al.'s Theorem 5.1 gives a bisection protocol (A states a middle configuration, B picks a half) deciding any time-T, space-S oracle computation with O(T log T) honest-prover time and O(1) oracle queries, restricting the honest prover to be efficient while the dishonest prover stays unbounded.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: recursive debate protocols for verifying long computations with few judge queries, from unbounded to polynomial-time honest provers

text: Theorem 5.1 states that any language decided by an oracle Turing machine in time T and space S has an (O(T log T), O(S log T), O(1))-debate protocol that deterministically decides it. In the protocol A outputs a claimed middle configuration of M(x) and B picks which half to recurse on, bottoming out in one transition checked by V; the authors contrast this with single-prover doubly-efficient interactive proofs that need O(S^2 polylog T) time and rely on the PCP theorem, which does not apply with a black-box oracle.
title: Theorem 5.1: deterministic debate verifies time-T, space-S computations with O(1) queries
